correctness.rationale: Solving the line-circle intersection gives the second complex endpoint −exp(i(2θ−φ)). Doubling a uniform unoriented angle gives Haar circle measure conditional on the entire past, not just on a fixed deterministic iterate. Hence the proposals are iid, and the exact full affine step picks the smaller objective, with no positive-probability ties. The start has maximum gap 2, and all iterates remain on the boundary. Tail integration with t=1+cos(πu) verifies the mean integral. The small-gap CDF and the bound F(t)≥sqrt(2t)/π give the distribution limit and the integrable dominating tail of mean π². At dyadic N, the lower-gap error is O(N^(−δ/2)) by a union bound and the upper-gap error is at most exp(−cN^(δ/2)); these are summable and monotonicity bridges dyadics. First passage is first success of the iid proposals. Insertion ranks bijectively encode each uniformly random full ranking, yielding independent Bernoulli(1/j) records; Bernstein on dyadics has summable tails at deviations ε log N, and monotonicity bridges these dyadics too. The local expected reduction is ∫_0^h F(t)dt; differentiating the closed form and using its zero initial value checks its normalization, and dividing by full-disk gap h gives the stated coefficient. Frozen verification notes and code were inspected; numerical and pairwise enumeration checks are diagnostics, not the proof of process independence or almost-sure laws. The result requires exact full steps, boundary initialization, independent Haar lines and an affine objective.

value.rationale: For a natural section-optimization model in exactly the direction dimension where uniform expected efficiency gives no rate, the identification supplies exact finite-horizon reliability, sharp N^−2 error and ε^−1/2 query constants, and a separate logarithmic cost in changed iterates. This is a tractable benchmark for an adaptive oracle with a vanishing uniform drift factor, not a claim of better general damped Frank–Wolfe convergence or novelty of classical record theory.
